instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes about 16 cups of chana masala or 8 (2-cup) servings.
TO SOAK THE CHICKPEAS: Place chickpeas in a large pot and cover with cold water. Let soak for a minimum of 8 hours (or overnight), at room temperature.

TO COOK THE CHICKPEAS: Drain soaked chickpeas, then return to the pot and cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil over high heat, skimming away any foam that rises to the surface. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 1 ½ hours. Remove from heat. Once the chickpeas have cooled slightly, carefully drain liquid from the beans (discard or save for another use) and set the cooked chickpeas aside.
TO MAKE THE CHANA MASALA: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (3 inch) piece ginger root
1 small bunch cilantro

instructions.primary_message: Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in a medium bowl.
Peel, halve, and small dice onions. Add to the bowl with the ginger and garlic.
Preheat a clean large pot over medium heat.

Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add ginger, garlic, onion, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is very soft, about 10 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp neutral vegetable oil
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, medium dice tomatoes. Place in the reserved bowl and set aside.

Quarter chili peppers lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level, then mince. (Be careful with chilis; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
When the onion is golden, add chili pepper and spices to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp garam masala
4 tsp coriander, ground
1 tbsp cumin, ground
2 ¼ tsp salt
2 tsp paprika
1 tsp turmeric, ground
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add cooked chickpeas, tomatoes, and broth to the pot, then stir to combine. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, uncover, reduce to a simmer, and cook, stirring occasionally, until chana masala has thickened slightly, 30-40 minutes.

When the chana masala is done, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add cilantro to the pot, stir to combine, and remove from heat. Set aside to cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally, about 30 minutes.
Once the chana masala has cooled, divide between containers.

STORING: Cover each container with an air-tight lid (or wrap tightly with plastic wrap). Place in the freezer for up to 3 months. HEATING: For best results, thaw chana masala in the fridge overnight. Warm in a saucepan set over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until heated through, about 5 minutes.
CHEF'S NOTE: Serve chana masala alongside rice or naan bread, topped with yogurt and more fresh cilantro if desired!
